column1: In the Application Insights schema, incoming DAB HTTP request telemetry is stored in {{c1::requests}}.
column2:
The requests table shows what reached the API, including endpoint name, duration, and success. Use dependencies for timed calls that DAB makes to other systems.
Review source

column1: In the Application Insights schema, recorded DAB calls to SQL and other external services appear in {{c1::dependencies}}.
column2:
A dependency record describes a call the API makes, such as a SQL operation. Compare its duration with the request duration to see whether SQL accounts for most of the delay.
Review source

column1: In the Application Insights schema, captured DAB exceptions and their call stacks appear in {{c1::exceptions}}.
column2:
The exceptions table contains exceptions that the instrumentation captured, including their details and stack information when available. A log message alone can appear in traces instead.
Review source

column1: The W3C HTTP header that carries a request's trace identity and parent context is {{c1::traceparent}}.
column2:
The header carries the trace identifier and the parent's span identifier. A downstream service can use that context to record its step as part of the same trace.
Review source

column1: In Application Insights, correlate an HTTP request with its SQL dependency records by matching their {{c1::operation_Id}} values.
column2:
Records with the same operation_Id belong to the same overall operation. Use it to find dependencies related to a request. Each individual record still has its own identifier.
Review source

column1: With Container Apps' direct Log Analytics integration, container stdout and stderr logs are stored in {{c1::ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL}}.
column2:
For direct Log Analytics integration, this table collects console output from the containers. Filter to the app or revision you are diagnosing before inspecting the message in Log_s.
Review source

column1: Limit an Application Insights query to the last hour with {{c1::where timestamp > ago(1h)}}.
column2:
The filter keeps rows whose timestamps are more recent than one hour ago. Apply it before calculating latency or error counts so the summary covers the intended incident window.
Review source

column1: For recorded Application Insights requests, calculate 95th-percentile latency with {{c1::percentile(duration, 95)}}.
column2:
P95 estimates the duration at or below which 95 percent of observations fall. It highlights slower requests that an average can hide. Use it inside summarize.
Review source

column1: To group Application Insights requests by endpoint, complete requests | summarize AvgDuration = avg(duration) {{c1::by name}}.
column2:
Grouping by name returns one average for each recorded request name. Without the grouping, summarize returns one average across all matching requests.
Review source

column1: In Application Insights queries, group telemetry into hourly time buckets with {{c1::bin(timestamp, 1h)}}.
column2:
The expression rounds each timestamp down to the start of its hour. Use it as a summarize grouping key to compare results hour by hour.
Review source

column1: If Application Insights captures SQL command text, that text can appear in the dependencies field {{c1::data}}.
column2:
The data field can contain the command if the instrumentation collects it. A dependency can record duration and success even when SQL text collection is disabled.
Review source

column1: In Application Insights dependencies, filter records classified as SQL calls with {{c1::where type == "SQL"}}.
column2:
Filter by the recorded dependency type before summarizing latency or failures. This leaves SQL dependency records rather than mixing them with HTTP calls or other dependency types.
Review source
